evidence.text: The present report suggests that biallelic EIF3K variants are associated with an autosomal recessive syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder. All individuals with homozygous EIF3K variants showed developmental delays, microcephaly, dysmorphic craniofacial features (Figure 3), digit flexion anomalies, PDA, and genitourinary malformations in males. Nearly all individuals had proportionate short stature and abnormal brain imaging. Our cohort included individuals 1-3, an aggregate cohort of <5 additional Puerto Rican individuals with the recurrent homozygous EIF3K missense variant c.128A>G, and individual 4 with the homozygous non-coding variant c.355-13A>G.

evidence.text: Patient 2 (P2) was a previously well 23-year-old male who presented with fevers and constitutional symptoms, extensive lymphadenopathy and pancytopenia. Biopsy of a lymph node demonstrated T-cell histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (THRLBCL) arising in a background of NLPHL, consistent with transformed disease. In addition, there were prominent background histological features resembling Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease. Bone marrow aspiration demonstrated marked haemophagocytosis with no morphological evidence of lymphoma. Treatment with DA-EPOCH-R was commenced with a near complete metabolic response achieved on interim FDG-PET. Targeted NGS (Methods S1) performed on DNA extracted from hair follicles identified a heterozygous frameshift TET2 variant (c.4781del; p.(Pro1594Leufs*2)). There was no family history of lymphoma or autoimmune disease, and family testing was not performed.
